# Results — Study 206 (Dividend-Aristocrats)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). NOBL (ProShares S&P 500
Dividend Aristocrats ETF) vs SPY (SPDR S&P 500 ETF), daily adjusted total-return closes,
2013-10-10 to 2026-06-15 (NOBL inception to present, n = 3,188 trading days ≈ 12.7 years).
All prices are `auto_adjust=True` (split/dividend-adjusted) from Yahoo Finance via yfinance.
As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| NOBL | 2013-10-10 → 2026-06-15 | 3,188 | `3834d744d492` |
| SPY  | 2013-10-09 → 2026-06-15 | 3,189 | `1012e7ad8d5b` |
| Aligned pair | 2013-10-10 → 2026-06-15 | 3,188 | `0d33bab56b32` |

NOBL tracks the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats Index (ProShares, ER = 0.35%/yr); SPY tracks
the S&P 500 (State Street, ER = 0.0945%/yr).  Both are total-return ETFs (dividends
reinvested automatically in the adjusted close series).

## The headline: NOBL vs SPY gross total-return (no ER adjustment)

| Metric | NOBL | SPY | Winner |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| **CAGR** | **+10.49%** | **+14.46%** | SPY by +3.97 pp |
| Annualised vol | 15.9% | 17.2% | NOBL (lower) |
| **Sharpe (gross, rf=0)** | **+0.629** | **+0.787** | **SPY** |
| Max drawdown | −35.4% | −33.7% | SPY (shallower) |
| Total return since inception | **253%** | **452%** | **SPY by 199 pp** |

NOBL is cheaper on vol (15.9% vs 17.2%) — a beta-of-0.81 effect, not an alpha.  Despite
lower volatility, NOBL's Sharpe *also* lags (0.629 vs 0.787): lower vol helped less than
lower return hurt.

## The honest signal test — excess return and OLS decomposition

### Excess return (NOBL − SPY daily log-return)

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| Mean excess return | **−1.40 bps/day** |
| Annualised CAGR differential | **−3.48%/yr** |
| HAC *t*-stat (Newey-West) | **−1.63** |
| Excess-return Sharpe 95% CI | **[−0.987, +0.088]** |
| Bootstrap resamples with negative excess Sharpe | **95%** |

The excess return is negative (−3.48%/yr) with a HAC *t* of −1.63: below the |*t*| = 2
inference bar, so **not significantly different from zero** — but pointedly on the *wrong*
side.  The bootstrap 95% CI on the excess Sharpe ([−0.99, +0.09]) barely clips above
zero, with 95% of resamples negative.  The null of zero excess return cannot be rejected
at conventional levels; the directional result is a clear underperformance.

### OLS alpha / beta decomposition

The "quality premium" claim predicts a positive market-neutral alpha.  OLS regression of
NOBL daily log-returns on SPY daily log-returns:

| Coefficient | Value | *t*-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Alpha (daily)** | **−0.38 bps/day** | **−0.45** |
| Alpha (annualised) | **−0.96%/yr** | — |
| **Beta** | **0.810** | — |
| R² | 0.767 | — |

Beta = 0.81 is the low-volatility/quality tilt in action: NOBL tracks the market but
participates less on both the upside and downside.  The OLS alpha is −0.38 bps/day
(−0.96%/yr) with *t* = −0.45 — statistically indistinguishable from zero, and on the
wrong side.  The quality factor premium, if it exists in this sample, is fully absorbed
by the lower beta.

## Net of expense ratios

After deducting NOBL's 0.35%/yr ER and SPY's 0.0945%/yr ER the gap widens:

| Metric | NOBL net | SPY net |
|---|--:|--:|
| CAGR | +10.10% | +14.36% |
| Sharpe | +0.607 | +0.782 |

The ER difference adds another ~0.26 pp/yr headwind for NOBL.

## Crash protection — does NOBL hold up better?

The "crash shield" claim is one of the strongest intuitive arguments for quality dividend
growers.  SPY drawdowns ≥ 15%:

| Episode | SPY max DD | SPY total ret (start→recovery) | NOBL total ret | NOBL protection |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Dec 2018 correction | −19.3% | +18.6% | +16.1% | **−2.5 pp** |
| COVID crash (Mar–Aug 2020) | −33.7% | +23.6% | +16.1% | **−7.6 pp** |
| 2022 bear market | −24.5% | +21.0% | +7.6% | **−13.4 pp** |
| Apr 2025 tariff shock | −18.8% | +21.5% | +6.2% | **−15.3 pp** |

NOBL underperformed SPY in *every* crash episode studied — the crash shield provided
**negative protection**.  This is the study's sharpest finding: not only did the
Aristocrats fail to outperform on returns, they also failed to deliver on the primary
investor justification (downside protection).  The COVID crash and 2022 were
particularly stark: quality/low-dividend-cut stocks did not buffer the falls.

## Could you trade it? — random-mix and scale

A random daily mix of NOBL and SPY (target weight 50% each, randomised ±50 pp per day
over 20 seeds) achieves a mean Sharpe of **+0.716** — better than pure NOBL (+0.629) in
100% of random seeds.  The "pure Aristocrats" concentration is strictly dominated by
any random mix, not just by the benchmark alone.

There are no capacity or turnover issues (both ETFs are liquid), but the ER headwind
(−0.26 pp vs SPY, −0.35 pp gross) is a perpetual drag with no gross alpha to offset it.

The tech-led 2023–2026 period accounts for most of the lifetime underperformance.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Excess-return HAC *t* = −1.63 (wrong sign), OLS alpha *t* = −0.45.
  No statistically robust quality/dividend-growth premium in NOBL's full live history.
  Negative alpha once low-beta is controlled.  The 2022 outperformance reversed sharply.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** NOBL costs 0.35%/yr more than SPY, delivers −3.97 pp/yr
  lower CAGR and a lower Sharpe despite lower volatility.  Negative crash protection in
  all four major drawdown episodes.  A random NOBL/SPY mix beats pure NOBL 100% of the
  time.
- **Crash shield? — Busted.** NOBL underperformed SPY inside every crash episode, with
  the largest underperformance in the most recent crises (−13.4 pp in 2022, −15.3 pp in
  Apr 2025).
